sarah (product): Quick sync — want to run a short bakeoff to settle scope + launch criteria for an economics-driven recommendations surface (batching, prefix/KV caching, quantization guidance) + eval-triggered alerts. Can we align on what 'MVP' actually means here?

mike (eng-runtime): I'm available. High-level: we should separate 'offline recommendations' (tuning params) vs 'live autosuggestions' in-console. Different risk and SLA.

kevin (ml): Agree. Also need to define acceptable quality loss for each quant profile. Some customers will accept -2% Rouge for 3x cost reduction; others won't.

jess (design): From UX perspective we need a single panel with clear cost delta, latency delta, and a confidence band. Keep it simple for first pass.

olivia (pm): Proposal: MVP shows recommended config per model/workload, predicted cost saving, expected latency impact, and an "Apply" button that triggers a canary. Launch criteria idea:
```
- Recommendation engine run on 3 canonical workloads
- Predicted unit-econ accuracy >= 80% vs offline sim
- UI shows cost/latency/confidence
- Canary flow + rollback implemented
- Eval-trigger alerts: regressions flagged on key prompt suites
```

sarah (product): Good checklist. Need to map customer asks. Tom, what have pilots been asking for?

tom (customer-success): Acme AI wants per-route batching suggestions and an "auto-batch" toggle. Beta customer B2Fin asked for KV-prefix cache suggestions for chat history. Both care about quantization but want a human-in-loop approval.

mike (eng-runtime): Implementation note: auto-batch is invasive — we should start with "suggested batch settings" and a simulator to show latency percentiles. Auto-apply can be a Q3 feature.

kevin (ml): For quantization we'd ship recommendations like: "8-bit hybrid (GPT-2 style) for short sequences, 4-bit for long-seq workloads" plus expected perplexity delta. Need offline eval harness before recommendations.

jess (design): Suggest we include a small explainer modal: "What this number means" for quality regressions and retry strategy. Non-technical PMs love that. :thumbsup:

olivia (pm): Prioritization ask: do we build eval-triggered alerts for launch or flag it as beta? Alerts are high value for customers who track regressions. My vote: minimal alerting (threshold-based) on day-one, advanced signal-driven alerts later.

mike (eng-runtime): Threshold-based alerting is lightweight: compare baseline metric to recommended-config metric on a daily window. We can integrate with existing alerting infra.

sarah (product): Let's pick hard launch gates:
1) Recommendation accuracy >= 80% on three pilot workloads (Acme, B2Fin, internal demo)
2) UI + canary apply + rollback in console
3) Alerting: threshold-based regression alerts wired to ops and product
4) Documentation + short runbook for customers

kevin (ml): Add: offline eval harness with reproducible seed and prompt suites must be in repo.

tom (customer-success): Also add a privacy check for Private deployments: no metric hashing/payload exfiltration.

mike (eng-runtime): Op note: we need a migration plan for customers already using custom batching logic. Don't break existing heuristics. Default to "opt-in".

jess (design): For MVP, UI flows: Recommendations tab -> per-route details -> simulate (latency/cost) -> Apply canary -> view canary metrics. Keep it to 4 screens.

olivia (pm): Timeline ask: can eng deliver the core recommender + simulator in 6 weeks? If not, push some UX polish to post-launch.

mike (eng-runtime): 6 weeks is tight but doable if we scope quantization recs as a ruleset rather than model-driven ML. Batching + caching sim + canary plumbing are priority.

sarah (product): Decision: ship batching + caching recommendations + threshold alerts + UI canary in MVP. Quantization guidance as ruleset (not ML recommender) in MVP; ML-driven quant recs targeted for post-MVP.

kevin (ml): Acknowledged. I'll prep the offline eval harness and the initial quant ruleset.

tom (customer-success): I'll coordinate with Acme/B2Fin for pilot signoff and runbook review.

jess (design): I'll mock the 4 screens and a short microcopy doc explaining "what to expect" for regressions.

mike (eng-runtime): I'll scope the simulator and canary rollback; will add a small CLI `ri-optimize simulate --route <r>` example for SREs.

sarah (product): Action items: @kevin: eval harness + quant ruleset; @mike: simulator + canary; @jess: mocks + copy; @tom: pilots; @olivia: finalize launch gates doc. Let's reconvene in 5 days with updated artifacts.

optimize-bot: Reminder — created a follow-up ticket: OPT-3421 (Optimize toolkit MVP - econ recs) assigned to ~team. :robot_face:

olivia (pm): Thanks all — quick check: any objections to the decision?

mike (eng-runtime): No objections.

kevin (ml): No objections.

jess (design): No objections.

tom (customer-success): No objections, will start scheduling pilot reviews.

sarah (product): Great — marking this thread resolved for now. We'll post the artifacts in the product drive when ready. :white_check_mark:
